item.title: Version 1.9.15
item.description:
Prices in the currency they say they're in

  • The Portfolio window converts the price columns. Last and Change printed the stock's native figure under your portfolio currency's symbol, while Value and P&L on the very same row were genuinely converted — a $190 holding read "€190" next to a real euro value. Both columns now carry the conversion.
  • Your average price is shown next to a comparable one. The 3×190 under a converted Last was still in the stock's own currency, so the two prices on a row could not be compared. It converts now, in the positions list and in the cross-portfolio view.
  • A price and its currency symbol can no longer disagree. Switching currency in Settings clears the exchange rates before fetching the new ones, and in that gap every price was printed unconverted under the new symbol. Prices now stay in the stock's own currency, symbol included, until the rate lands — then switch over on their own. A dropped rate request is retried instead of stranding the display until the next poll.
  • The average price field names its currency. It has always been stored in the stock's own currency whatever the display settings say, but the field just said "Avg price" — so people converted the figure by hand before typing it in, and it was counted twice. It now reads "Avg price (USD)".

Arrange the watchlist from the menu bar

  • The compact list opens in your own order. It always sorted by the day's change and offered no way back, so the order you had arranged in the main window was unreachable there.
  • Drag a row to move it, or use Move Up / Move Down from the right-click menu — the same actions the main window has. Dragging is withheld while a column sort or a search filter is active, so a drag can never move the wrong row.
  • A column sort is no longer a one-way door. Clicking a header a third time returns to your own order.

With thanks to Indianhedgehog and nez329, whose issues drove this release.
